commenti.body:
Entertainment. A film doesn’t necessarily have to be of great quality as long as it keeps my attention. 

I used to work at a video store for years and I’ve found that most people rent films for pretty much the same reason. Simply to be entertained

I consume stories in whatever form they take. Movies, books, reddit posts, my friends shitty rambling story. I dont know why. I just take them in. Some stick in my head and some get forgotten instantly.
It's like playing with toys, as children do, but with ideas.
Did you come up with that?

We come to this place for magic. We come to the movies to love, to cry, to care. Because we need that, all of us. That indescribable feeling you get when the lights begin to dim. And we go somewhere we’ve never been before. Not just entertained but somehow reborn, together. Dazzling images on a huge silver screen. Sound that I can feel. Somehow heartbreak feels good in a place like this. Our heroes feel like the best part of us, and stories feel perfect and powerful. Because here, they are.

It's not JUST entertainment for me. Film is my favorite style of art as it combines so many other forms of art like visual art, music, writing, spoken word, design, performance. I often engage with film the same way I engage with other forms of art. I like to think about an analyze movies from that stand point. I like to explore other cultures. I like to see and hear stories. 

And sometimes I really do like to be entertained.
Because I get bored.
Because they're interesting.

Comfort- I love background noise and replaying shows where  I know what will happen in the background as I do other things helps my anxiety a lot by drowning out other noise and helps me feel more in control of my environment. 
  
Also to feel things- if I’m sad I’ll watch a sad movie to help get it out, comedy to cheer up, etc. 
  
Social- if I’m hanging with someone I don’t know as well I’ll put on a movie or show to give us something to talk about if things ever get too quiet

I think people as animals need to feel these emotions., and we feel we no longer can in real life or are losing the skills/desire to. It's like an imitation of life within life. So I watch it to escape the real life.

I put movies and TV shows on for background noise the same way people would listen to the radio. I prefer the addition of visuals to just sound, and I like there to be a story to entertain me. I prefer TV because my favourite part of a story is the characterization, and there’s more time to develop a character in TV than there is in a movie. 

In terms of putting on a movie for not background noise, again I am typically story focused. I like things that are thoughtful and interesting, a story that will maintain my focus and surprise me along the way. Not a horror, with thrill jumps, but the story itself.
I had a blah childhood; movies (along with TV & video games) were my respite.
To avoid doing things that actually might make my own life better

It is a strong part of my cultural upbringing. I grew up in extreme poverty but we had two small movie theaters in town that were really cheap to get into. And most importantly, they had heat and air conditioning, which our house did not. So we would save up some money and spend the entire day at the movies watching whatever was playing. Then every time we got gas, we would get a free movie rental at a small local market. So we could save those up to watch at home because other than reading stacks of books from the library, there was nothing else to do. As I grew older, my tradition of watching movies continued.

I don’t watch very many in fact I haven’t seen any this year so far but when I do I go for things that seem to have a great plot great acting and great visually.  I LOVE when it is great visually seeing that on the big screen esp.
I love the whole movie experience the popcorn or sweets (candy, lollies) the plush seats it’s more luxurious than watching something at home.  
I am happy to see movies alone also if I don’t like it I can leave.  But when I have seen movies with someone and liked the movie it’s fun to chat about it after.  Movies can be funny, romantic, suspenseful even all of the above and more.  If I like the franchise or know another version it’s fun to see it on the big screen or see it continued.  Like the newest ghostbusters I skipped seeing the 2016 one I DO usually read reviews before I decide! 
Or like Lord of the Rings I read the book before I saw the movie.  Ditto Death on the Nile.  Seeing an actor or actress whose a fave is fun too. 
Lots of reasons!
I tend to only see a few movies a year though but it’s usually something I REALLY want to see.
Sometimes for entertainment (action movies) , most of the time for thinking (dramas). But after watching drama movies I usually feel like shit, so it seems like I watch them to torture myself.
I love forgetting about real life and being immersed inside a different world (even if it’s a historical movie/true story etc, I still forget about my own problems while in the movie)

Because I enjoy them. There really is nothing more to it than that. I find movies enjoyable in a similar way that I find music enjoyable: it makes me feel something different than what I would feel without it.
Movies capture what you want to say or do but don't think of at the time or don't have the courage to put out there. That's to boil it down.
Movie really stands for move me
Thank you for your answer, friend!

Sometimes to escape reality (i.e entertainment), other times to learn a bit about different cultures or certain historical events, etc. When i'm drunk i like to watch stuff from my childhood, because i get nostalgic

- As an escape from ‘real’ world
- interested in the stories & concepts explored by movies and the directors interpretation of it
